title.justification: This is the paper title printed at the beginning of the supplied text.
title.value: A Survey on Deep Learning for Theorem Proving

extractions.description: A non-experimental survey that organizes prior work on deep learning for theorem proving, including autoformalization, premise selection, proofstep generation, proof search, datasets, synthetic-data strategies, and evaluation. It reports no compute runs of its own.

type.quote: This paper presents a comprehensive survey of deep learning for theorem proving
type.justification: The work synthesizes prior literature rather than reporting a new experiment; it is best classified as theoretical/non-empirical under the available two-way schema.

name.justification: The phrase directly names the survey's central research area.

name.quote: Formal theorem proving represents theorems and proofs in a machine-verifiable format
name.justification: Formal theorem proving is a major field surveyed and structured by the paper.

name.quote: Autoformalization aims to convert informal theorems and proofs into machine-verifiable formats automatically.
name.justification: The survey treats autoformalization as one of its principal research areas.

name.quote: premise selection is to retrieve the helpful lemmas that can contribute to a successful proof
name.justification: Premise selection is one of the principal areas reviewed by the survey.
